claims.text: The rider's account is made out on the platform's own recorded distances, not on any reconstruction: EV-TRIP-00902 records 24.8 km actually driven against 20.5 km on the recommended route, a deviation of 4.30 km. Under POL-RD-22 that subtraction is the deviation, and 4.30 km is far outside the 1.0 km tolerance, so the rider was in fact taken materially further than the recommended Orchard Central - Changi T3 route.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log carries six entries and not one message from the driver announces a route change: the driver's only messages are pre-trip pleasantries at 13:09 and 13:10:30 (MSG-00902-002, MSG-00902-004). The first word about the route comes from the rider at 13:24 - 'are we going the right way?' - and the driver's answer at 13:25, 'Don't worry, I know the way', names no deviation and offers no reason. EV-TRIP-00902's derived messages_during_trip contains only those two exchanges, and with no call recording in the record a verbal notice cannot be established at all under POL-GEN-26.

On the refund matrix, row (b) applies and the rider is owed the excess distance fare. Even accepting that the PIE advisories justified a reroute under POL-RD-23, the driver did not inform the rider and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so row (b) returns the excess distance fare. POL-RD-24's escalation example is the case where the rider was informed and objected; here there was no notice at all, so the case falls squarely in row (b) and does not slip through to escalation.

The amount of that refund is fixed by the policy formula and the ledger: 4.30 km of deviation times the per-kilometre rate of 0.80 SGD gives 3.44 SGD, with no surge added (POL-RD-24). EV-FARE-00902 carries both the rate and the resulting excess_distance_fare_sgd of 3.44, and shows the rider was charged 35.00 against a 28.50 quote with the charge sitting at payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 - so the rider is still carrying the excess the deviation created.

The advisory for the route the driver actually took furnishes no justification of its own: TC-003 describes the ECP as flowing smoothly with no incidents, its type TRAFFIC_FLOW is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 admits (closure, congestion, incident), and it does not intersect the recommended route. So if traffic justification is contested there is no support on the driver's own line either; whether the case falls in row (b) or row (d), POL-RD-24 returns the same excess distance fare to the rider, and no row returns the rider nothing.

The rider's deviation case places no weight on the GPS trace, and the rider says so rather than dressing it up: EV-GPS-00902 is IMPAIRED on the issue code LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at a weight multiplier of 0.8, ten of its fifteen intervals exceed the 120 s limb, and POL-RD-22 expressly forbids re-measuring the route from a sparse trace because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The distances that carry the 4.30 km deviation come from EV-TRIP-00902, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The refund should issue now rather than being held: the sum in dispute, 6.50 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag (both record 0), there is no safety flag, and POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit is not applied on this version - so the AI ruling on this route deviation is final and a refund is payable to the rider rather than the charge being held on escalation.

claims.text: The reroute was traffic-justified, which defeats the rider's premise that the extra distance was a gratuitous detour. Advisory TC-001 records a vehicle fire on the PIE eastbound (HIGH severity, lanes 1 and 2 blocked) that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and TC-002 records heavy congestion at the PIE's Changi Airport exit ramp over the same window. VEHICLE_FIRE and HEAVY_CONGESTION are the kinds of condition POL-RD-23 names, and POL-RD-21 expressly permits a driver to reroute in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion. The case therefore belongs in POL-RD-24's traffic-justified branch, and the rider cannot be heard to insist on the recommended route while it was obstructed by a fire and its congestion.

The notification fact is the only thing standing between the driver and no refund, and this record does not settle it. The complete chat log shows the rider raising the route in-app at 13:24 and the driver answering at 13:25, and no in-app explanation of a deviation appears (MSG-005, MSG-006); no call recording exists. But POL-RD-21 permits a verbal notice at the wheel, which by its nature leaves no record, and the clause itself provides that a verbal notice with no recording in the record 'cannot be established', pointing to POL-GEN-26; the driver's own account is not on file (counterparty_statement is null). 'Whether the driver notified the rider' is the first fact POL-GEN-26 names, so an unestablished notification escalates rather than yielding a refund on the rider's account alone. And if the driver's 13:25 reply is treated as notice of a route choice the rider had already challenged, the case is POL-RD-24's express catch-all - informed but the rider objected - which also escalates. Either way the outcome is human review with the amount held under POL-GEN-03, not money refunded on the papers.

Even on the rider's own case, the sum she asks for is not one the policy provides. POL-RD-24's only fare measure is the excess distance fare: the deviation is the platform's recorded difference, 24.8 minus 20.5 = 4.30 km under POL-RD-22, and at the recorded rate of 0.80 per km that is 3.44 SGD, with no surge. The rider instead asks for the 6.50 SGD gap between the 35.00 charged and the 28.50 quote. The ledger (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, no issue codes) itemises no base, time or platform-fee line and states nothing beyond the aggregate 35.00, so nothing in it supports a figure above 3.44. The claim for 6.50 is therefore beyond what this policy can award.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider's fare is partly returned, and the amount is fixed by the route-deviation policy, not by the difference between the quoted and the charged fare.

What is established. The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-00902, complete at weight 1.0) records 24.8 km driven against 20.5 km on the recommended Orchard Central - Changi T3 route. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is that subtraction: 4.30 km, well outside the 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 does not re-measure the route from the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00902 is impaired at weight 0.8 on LOW_SAMPLE_RATE; a sparse trace understates a route's length), so the trace is not relied on and its impairment does not enter this ruling.

The reroute was traffic-justified. TC-001 (EV-ADVIS-00902-01) records a HIGH-severity vehicle fire on the PIE eastbound with lanes 1 and 2 blocked, intersecting the recommended route and inside the trip window, and TC-002 (EV-ADVIS-00902-02) records heavy congestion at the PIE's Changi Airport exit ramp over the same window. Both are of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (incident, congestion) and both intersect the route and overlap the trip. The driver was entitled to reroute (POL-RD-21).

The driver did not inform the rider. The complete, contiguous chat log (EV-CHAT-00902, weight 1.0) contains no message announcing a route change: the driver's only messages before the rider's query are pre-trip pleasantries (13:09, 13:10:30). The rider raises the route herself at 13:24 ('are we going the right way?'), and the driver's 13:25 reply, 'Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.', names no deviation and gives no reason, so it is not the notice POL-RD-21 requires. No call recording exists. That makes the driver's notification the only open question to test.

On the refund matrix. The case is POL-RD-24 row (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km. The measure is the excess distance fare: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD per km (EV-FARE-00902) = 3.44 SGD, with no surge. That is why the rider's figure of 6.50 SGD is not awarded: the policy's route-deviation refund is the excess distance fare (POL-RD-24), not the 35.00 charged less the 28.50 quote. The driver's own submission to the same effect is accepted. Row (d) (not traffic-justified) would pay the same 3.44 SGD, so nothing turns on which justification branch applies.

Why this is not escalated. The driver argues that because a verbal notice at the wheel leaves no record, 'whether the driver notified the rider' cannot be established and POL-GEN-26 requires human review, or alternatively that the driver's 13:25 reply was notice to a rider who objected (POL-RD-24's catch-all). Neither succeeds. The evidence that carries the notification fact - the chat log - is present, complete and unimpaired; it shows no notice, so the fact is established in the negative rather than missing. POL-RD-21 makes an unrecorded verbal notice incapable of satisfying the driver's obligation, and the driver here asserted none (no counterparty statement on file). Reading every no-notice case as unestablished would make row (b), the clause's own provision for exactly this situation, a dead letter. The catch-all does not apply because the driver never informed the rider in the first place.

Confidence and authority. POL-RD-25 requires 0.80 and the deciding facts rest on artifacts all at weight 1.0 (trip record, chat log, fare ledger, both route advisories), so the cap allows 0.85. The value in dispute, 6.50 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag, there is no safety flag, and POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit is not applied on this version, so the AI ruling is final and the refund issues rather than the charge being held. No clause of the route-deviation policy produces a referral on these facts.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is the decision on DISP-001.

Deviation (POL-RD-22). The platform's own trip record, EV-TRIP-00902 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0), records 24.8 km actually driven against 20.5 km on the recommended Orchard Central–Changi T3 route. That subtraction is the deviation, 4.30 km, far outside the 1.0 km tolerance. The rider's account on this point is accepted. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00902 (weight 0.8, issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE) is not relied on: POL-RD-22 forbids re-measuring the route from a sparse trace, and neither side asks it to, so its impairment does not hold this ruling's confidence down.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). TC-001 (vehicle fire, PIE eastbound, HIGH) and TC-002 (heavy congestion at the PIE/airport exit, MODERATE) each intersect the recommended route and overlap the trip window, so the reroute was traffic-justified. The driver's first claim is accepted: the rider's premise of a gratuitous detour fails. TC-003 (ECP, TRAFFIC_FLOW) justifies nothing on its own, but nothing turns on it.

Notification (POL-RD-21). The driver had to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording, before or at the point of deviation. The complete chat log EV-CHAT-00902 (weight 1.0) carries no such notice: the pre-trip messages are pleasantries, and when the rider asked at 13:24 "are we going the right way?" the driver's 13:25 answer gave no reason and named no deviation. With no call recording in the record, and the obligation resting on the driver, the rider was not informed. The rider's second claim is accepted; the driver's argument that this fact is unestablished (POL-GEN-26) is rejected — the chat log is present, complete and its own reading is decisive.

Refund (POL-RD-24). The case falls in row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km) — and equally in row (d), which returns the same figure. The refund is the excess distance fare: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD/km = 3.44 SGD, with no surge. EV-FARE-00902 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) carries the 0.80 rate and the 3.44 excess figure, and shows the rider charged 35.00 against a 28.50 quote with 0.00 refunded so far. The rider asked for 6.50 SGD, the gap between the 35.00 charged and the 28.50 quote; POL-RD-24 provides only the excess distance fare, so the request is granted in part only, as the driver's third claim correctly observes.

Why the AI decides rather than escalates: the disputed value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0; there is no safety flag; and POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit is not applied on this policy version. The ruling's confidence meets POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar.

Outcome: 3.44 SGD is refunded to the rider (the part of the 6.50 SGD contested that the policy provides); no sum is payable to the driver, and no referral arises, as route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your account is made out on the platform's own recorded distances. EV-TRIP-00902 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records 24.8 km actually driven against 20.5 km on the recommended Orchard Central – Changi T3 route. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is that subtraction — 4.30 km — which is outside the 1.0 km tolerance, and the trace is not used to re-measure the distance (POL-RD-22). You are therefore right that you were taken materially further than the recommended route, and you are owed the excess distance fare. But you are not owed the 6.50 SGD you asked for. The 6.50 is the gap between the 35.00 charged and the 28.50 quote; POL-RD-24's only fare measure is the excess distance fare, which is the deviation times the recorded per-km rate: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD = 3.44 SGD, with no surge (EV-FARE-00902, weight 1.0, excess_distance_fare_sgd 3.44).

To the driver: the reroute was in fact traffic-justified under POL-RD-23 — EV-ADVIS-00902-01 (VEHICLE_FIRE on the PIE eastbound, HIGH, lanes 1 and 2 blocked) and EV-ADVIS-00902-02 (HEAVY_CONGESTION at the PIE airport exit) both intersect the recommended route and overlap the trip window, and their types are among those the clause admits. That part of your case is accepted. What defeats you is notification. POL-RD-21 requires you to inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, by in-app chat or verbally with a call recording. The chat log is complete (EV-CHAT-00902, weight 1.0): it carries only pre-trip pleasantries from you and no message announcing a route change. The first word on the route is the rider's at 13:24, and your 13:25 reply ('Don't worry, I know the way') names no deviation and gives no reason. No call recording exists, so a verbal notice cannot be established (POL-RD-21, POL-GEN-26). That places the case in POL-RD-24 row (b) — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — which returns the excess distance fare of 3.44 SGD. Your argument that the notification fact is unestablished and the case must escalate is rejected: the clause makes the chat log the test for notification, that log is complete and shows no notice, and the clause's own words resolve a recording-less verbal notice to 'not established'. It does not create an open question, and it is not POL-RD-24's 'informed but objected' catch-all, because no notice was given at all. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00902, IMPAIRED, LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8) is not used to measure the deviation and plays no part here.

No referral applies on a route deviation in this version. The dispute value of 6.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag is present on either profile, POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit is not applied on this version, and the ruling's confidence is above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires, so the AI ruling is final. Amounts used: deviation 4.30 km, per-km rate 0.80 SGD, excess distance fare 3.44 SGD, contested amount 6.50 SGD.

ledger.claim: The rider's account is made out on the platform's own recorded distances, not on any reconstruction: EV-TRIP-00902 records 24.8 km actually driven against 20.5 km on the recommended route, a deviation of 4.30 km. Under POL-RD-22 that subtraction is the deviation, and 4.30 km is far outside the 1.0 km tolerance, so the rider was in fact taken materially further than the recommended Orchard Central - Changi T3 route.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log carries six entries and not one message from the driver announces a route change: the driver's only messages are pre-trip pleasantries at 13:09 and 13:10:30 (MSG-00902-002, MSG-00902-004). The first word about the route comes from the rider at 13:24 - 'are we going the right way?' - and the driver's answer at 13:25, 'Don't worry, I know the way', names no deviation and offers no reason. EV-TRIP-00902's derived messages_during_trip contains only those two exchanges, and with no call recording in the record a verbal notice cannot be established at all under POL-GEN-26.

On the refund matrix, row (b) applies and the rider is owed the excess distance fare. Even accepting that the PIE advisories justified a reroute under POL-RD-23, the driver did not inform the rider and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so row (b) returns the excess distance fare. POL-RD-24's escalation example is the case where the rider was informed and objected; here there was no notice at all, so the case falls squarely in row (b) and does not slip through to escalation.

The amount of that refund is fixed by the policy formula and the ledger: 4.30 km of deviation times the per-kilometre rate of 0.80 SGD gives 3.44 SGD, with no surge added (POL-RD-24). EV-FARE-00902 carries both the rate and the resulting excess_distance_fare_sgd of 3.44, and shows the rider was charged 35.00 against a 28.50 quote with the charge sitting at payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 - so the rider is still carrying the excess the deviation created.

The advisory for the route the driver actually took furnishes no justification of its own: TC-003 describes the ECP as flowing smoothly with no incidents, its type TRAFFIC_FLOW is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 admits (closure, congestion, incident), and it does not intersect the recommended route. So if traffic justification is contested there is no support on the driver's own line either; whether the case falls in row (b) or row (d), POL-RD-24 returns the same excess distance fare to the rider, and no row returns the rider nothing.

The rider's deviation case places no weight on the GPS trace, and the rider says so rather than dressing it up: EV-GPS-00902 is IMPAIRED on the issue code LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at a weight multiplier of 0.8, ten of its fifteen intervals exceed the 120 s limb, and POL-RD-22 expressly forbids re-measuring the route from a sparse trace because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The distances that carry the 4.30 km deviation come from EV-TRIP-00902, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The refund should issue now rather than being held: the sum in dispute, 6.50 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag (both record 0), there is no safety flag, and POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit is not applied on this version - so the AI ruling on this route deviation is final and a refund is payable to the rider rather than the charge being held on escalation.

The reroute was traffic-justified, which defeats the rider's premise that the extra distance was a gratuitous detour. Advisory TC-001 records a vehicle fire on the PIE eastbound (HIGH severity, lanes 1 and 2 blocked) that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and TC-002 records heavy congestion at the PIE's Changi Airport exit ramp over the same window. VEHICLE_FIRE and HEAVY_CONGESTION are the kinds of condition POL-RD-23 names, and POL-RD-21 expressly permits a driver to reroute in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion. The case therefore belongs in POL-RD-24's traffic-justified branch, and the rider cannot be heard to insist on the recommended route while it was obstructed by a fire and its congestion.

The notification fact is the only thing standing between the driver and no refund, and this record does not settle it. The complete chat log shows the rider raising the route in-app at 13:24 and the driver answering at 13:25, and no in-app explanation of a deviation appears (MSG-005, MSG-006); no call recording exists. But POL-RD-21 permits a verbal notice at the wheel, which by its nature leaves no record, and the clause itself provides that a verbal notice with no recording in the record 'cannot be established', pointing to POL-GEN-26; the driver's own account is not on file (counterparty_statement is null). 'Whether the driver notified the rider' is the first fact POL-GEN-26 names, so an unestablished notification escalates rather than yielding a refund on the rider's account alone. And if the driver's 13:25 reply is treated as notice of a route choice the rider had already challenged, the case is POL-RD-24's express catch-all - informed but the rider objected - which also escalates. Either way the outcome is human review with the amount held under POL-GEN-03, not money refunded on the papers.

Even on the rider's own case, the sum she asks for is not one the policy provides. POL-RD-24's only fare measure is the excess distance fare: the deviation is the platform's recorded difference, 24.8 minus 20.5 = 4.30 km under POL-RD-22, and at the recorded rate of 0.80 per km that is 3.44 SGD, with no surge. The rider instead asks for the 6.50 SGD gap between the 35.00 charged and the 28.50 quote. The ledger (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, no issue codes) itemises no base, time or platform-fee line and states nothing beyond the aggregate 35.00, so nothing in it supports a figure above 3.44. The claim for 6.50 is therefore beyond what this policy can award.
